memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text:
"Redeem with a lamb every firstborn donkey, but if you do not redeem it, break
its neck. Redeem every firstborn among your sons." - Ex 13:13 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This verse sounds strange to us, so let us take it slowly.

A donkey was an unclean animal under the law and could not be sacrificed. Yet it
belonged to God as a firstborn. So a lamb died in its place, and the donkey went
free. If the owner refused to provide a lamb, the donkey could not simply be
kept as though God had no claim.

Then comes the line that matters most: "Redeem every firstborn among your sons."
Israel's sons were not sacrificed. God utterly forbids that (Deut 12:31). They
were bought back, at a price, by a substitute.

Sit with the picture. An unclean animal with no worth in itself, spared because
a spotless lamb died instead. That is not a strained allegory; it is the shape of
redemption running right through Scripture.

Peter uses the very word: we were redeemed "with the precious blood of Christ, a
lamb without blemish or defect" (1 Pet 1:19). Not silver. Not gold. Not our own
improvement.

Every Israelite father who handed over a lamb for his son was rehearsing
something. Generations later, a Father would not withhold His own Son (Rom
8:32).

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Have you understood that you were bought, not merely forgiven?
2. What does it mean that a price was paid for you?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text:
Lord Jesus, You are the Lamb who took my place. Thank You that I was redeemed at
the cost of Your blood. Amen.
